## release: promote develop → main (pinned `b47acfdb9e`)

Operator-authorized launch promotion of the current develop tip to production main. **367 commits** since the last promote (`ff751c2857`, #18028, 2026-08-08).

**Pinned to `b47acfdb9e`** — this PR promotes exactly this SHA. Its CI run certifies the frozen SHA independent of develop churn (the last 11 develop CI runs were superseded/cancelled before finishing, so the moving develop head had **zero** certified-green runs; this pinned PR fixes that).

topPRs.body:

<!-- attribution-row:status -->
- Provenance status: `self-reported`

# Sync with develop

- [x] Rebased onto `origin/develop` at `3bd3b34f6ac97a7861a5de903c72e7e089adc620`; the only conflict was the paired plugin-mcp guide, resolved by preserving upstream env-declared server support and this branch's corrected resource-engine/retry contract.
- [x] `bun run verify` passes post-sync on Bun 1.3.14 and Node 24.15.0.

# Risks

**Large.** This changes Google OAuth secret handling, agent authorization, connector migration, runtime tool materialization, and the execution protocol for personal Gmail/Calendar/Drive/Docs/Sheets/Slides/People/Chat/Search. The main mitigations are vault-only durable secrets, per-call binding/scope rechecks, curated exact tool allowlists, fail-closed unsupported operations, a sole-agent-only migration backfill, and explicit multi-agent rebinding.

Google Workspace MCP remains Developer Preview. Gmail is intentionally draft-only because the official server has no send tool. Calendar is intentionally read-only because current MCP event schemas do not provide the idempotency and atomic version preconditions required by existing LifeOps write guarantees.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Adds a stateless MCP v2 remote-resource engine with exact calls, pagination, SSRF validation, opaque attachment generations, and injected short-lived access-token providers.
- Replaces personal Google REST execution with Google's official per-product MCP endpoints.
- Uses one direct authorization-code OAuth flow. OAuth app secrets, refresh/access tokens, and PKCE verifiers are stored behind vault/secret references; raw refresh tokens are not serialized into MCP config.
- Separates a reusable OAuth account from per-agent bindings. Bindings own selected products, allowed capabilities, default selection, status, and independent revocation.
- Dynamically materializes only reviewed namespaced tools and removes them when a product, capability, scope, binding, or connection is removed.
- Makes Cloud call official Google resources directly from its trusted runtime and revalidates the current binding, product, capability, tool, and scopes before bearer injection. The old Google broker/stub routes are removed.
- Thins `plugin-google-workspace` to OAuth, vault resolution, the multi-resource capability host, stable typed adapters, and the separate service-account Google Chat connector.
- Removes personal Google REST clients, Calendar watch/webhook infrastructure, Meet REST artifacts, Gmail Watch registry data, legacy Mockoon/REST fixtures, and old Gmail compatibility scenario contracts.
- Migrates Gmail/Calendar scenarios to deterministic MCP fixtures and exact call ledgers. Unsupported spam/bulk/send/calendar-write behavior is asserted to fail closed.
- Regenerates Cloud routes/SDK wrappers and the first-party plugin registry.

This PR completes the personal Google Workspace MCP-only cutover. It does not implement the broader Linear/Notion/GitHub SaaS deletion wave from the long-term portfolio plan.

## What kind of change is this?

Features, improvements, security hardening, database migration, and intentional removal of obsolete connector compatibility surfaces.

# Documentation changes needed?

Documentation was updated for the direct OAuth/vault/binding model, official MCP endpoints, draft-only Gmail, read-only Calendar, removed broker/watch/mock surfaces, and the service-account Chat exception.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

1. `packages/shared/src/contracts/google-workspace-mcp.ts` — canonical endpoint/tool/scope policy.
2. `plugins/plugin-mcp/src/resource-engine.ts` — stateless authenticated exact-call engine.
3. `plugins/plugin-google-workspace/src/mcp/capability-host.ts` and `src/service.ts` — local dynamic capabilities and typed adapters.
4. `packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/eliza/runtime/mcp-config.ts` and `lib/eliza/plugin-mcp/service.ts` — Cloud fan-out and per-call authorization.
5. `packages/cloud/api/v1/eliza/agents/[agentId]/connectors` — binding CRUD/revocation.
6. `packages/ui/src/components/connectors` and `packages/ui/src/cloud/instances/components/eliza-agent-connectors-section.tsx` — product selection and agent binding UX.

## Detailed testing steps

- `bun install` — pass.
- `bun run verify` — pass after rebase (348/348 Turbo tasks plus repository audits).
- `plugins/plugin-mcp`: 73 passed, 3 skipped.
- `plugins/plugin-google-workspace`: 56 passed.
- `packages/scenario-runner`: 385 passed.
- `packages/shared`: 1,371 passed.
- `plugins/plugin-calendar`: 482 passed, 4 skipped.
- Focused connector UI: 12 passed.
- Cloud binding/config/security/migration group: 25 passed.
- Cloud binding revoke/OAuth callback group: 11 passed.
- Cloud OAuth provider registry: 9 passed.
- Cloud SDK: 79 passed, 19 live tests skipped.
- Cloud route audit: 515/515 public wrappers, 0 missing, 0 stale, 0 outside public scope.
- Registry: 37 passed; generated artifacts current.
- Test corpus: 3,410 scenarios validated.
- `bun run --cwd packages/app audit:app`: 214/215 checks passed. Affected Settings captures are all `good`; Calendar has no `broken` or `needs-work` verdict. The command exits nonzero only for unrelated existing minimalism-ratchet breaches in Browser, Plugins, and Trajectories views.

<!-- evidence-row:backend-logs -->

<!-- evidence-row:frontend-logs -->

<!-- evidence-row:domain-artifacts -->

<!-- evidence-row:ocr-review -->

# Evidence Details

## Real LLM-call trajectory

N/A for this draft run: a real trajectory requires a consented Google test account. No credential was available, and no synthetic run is represented as live evidence.

## Backend + frontend logs

Deterministic test output proves vault resolution, OAuth callback binding, per-agent revoke, migration backfill, product/scope narrowing, exact endpoint/tool authorization, and disconnect removal. Live OAuth network and UI logs remain pending.

## Screenshots (before / after) + video walkthrough

Local app-audit captures were reviewed for Settings and Calendar across desktop, mobile portrait, mobile landscape, and iPad. They are not yet uploaded. This is the primary reason the PR remains a draft.

## Known gaps / failures

- Google Workspace MCP is Developer Preview and no live Google test credential was available. Contract tests use reviewed official schemas and deterministic MCP fixtures, not fabricated live success.
- `audit:app` exits nonzero on four unrelated minimalism ratchets in Browser, Plugins, and Trajectories. The affected Settings views are all `good`; Calendar has no `broken` or `needs-work` verdict.
- The monolithic personal-assistant Vitest lane has an existing worktree resolution failure for `@elizaos/core/testing` in unrelated suites. Affected Google scope/access/scenario tests, package typecheck/build, root verification, and the cross-package scenario runner all pass.
- Live screenshots, MP4, OCR attachment, backend logs, frontend logs, and real model trajectory must be added before changing this PR from draft to ready.
- The wider non-Google SaaS connector portfolio migration is explicitly out of scope.

topPRs.title: fix(cloud): restore dedicated-agent pairing session
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
Closes #18304.

## Outcome

This restores the managed dedicated-agent **Open → pair → authenticated app** path and closes the credential-boundary holes found while tracing the original “expired link” failure.

- The Hetzner router preserves the Worker-pinned public agent host instead of replacing it with the control-plane host.
- Managed pairing terminates at the Cloud Worker, claims the one-time token atomically against the exact agent and origin, and writes only an owner-scoped browser credential.
- Remote containers cannot re-enable the direct pairing relay; local Docker retains an explicit loopback-only compatibility mode.
- Pre-auth managed HTML never contains the full agent bearer.
- The dedicated-agent proxy strips Cloud cookies/credential headers, rejects authenticated non-owners, owns CORS, strips response cookies/site-clearing headers, preserves WebSocket upgrades, and removes every Cloud-shaped realtime query credential before forwarding.
- UI restore/switch paths bind credentials to UUID agent owners and trusted bases, use an atomic base+token WebSocket repoint, never send Steward credentials to loopback, and make profile persistence failure visible instead of reporting a false successful switch.

## Exact object

- head: `eafcf934029264e75f55731a75c35eddf2a3f023`
- tree: `0e787ba60278d79f129d1794263063df5940b54c`
- base: `86c1d685270ba33ace21df5a080a22f95dc030cb` (`origin/develop`, 0 behind)
- commits: 12
- scope: 77 files, +5130 / -965

## Verification

- `bun run verify`: PASS — Turbo 348/348 plus all trailing audits; 0 focused/orphaned tests.
- focused UI/session suites: 17 files / 231 tests PASS.
- focused live-Worker Group A auth E2E: 47/47 PASS; the pairing cases reach their intended missing-token, missing-Origin, and invalid-token branches.
- real Chromium pairing evidence: 2/2 PASS — production relay/storage/boot-adopter modules, visible fail-closed recovery, and zero bearer persistence on invalid ownership.
- focused dedicated Worker proxy suite: 39/39 tests, 187 assertions PASS.
- Cloud pairing/router/atomic-claim/remote-runtime suites: PASS, including real PGlite claim coverage.
- package typechecks: UI, Cloud API, Cloud shared, agent, app-core, shared PASS.
- Cloudflare Worker production dry-run bundle: PASS.
- Biome on every changed path and `git diff --check`: PASS.
- `bun run --cwd packages/app audit:app`: 214/215; all affected Runtime, Settings, Cloud, and Cockpit surfaces passed across mobile/desktop/iPad. The only failure is four Browser/Plugins/Trajectories minimalism-density ratchets outside this PR’s diff; no visual baseline was changed.

## Staging history and release boundary

The router-only staging deployment already proved a fresh link reaches `/pair`, exposing the second owner-scoped handoff bug fixed here. Every earlier d26, e40, and e286 image is explicitly superseded and must not be used for final QA.

Run [31436242422](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/31436242422) succeeded on exact head eafcf934. The real production entrypoint reached ready/responding with runtime and database healthy, 23 plugins loaded / 0 failed, deferred boot settled, 15 seconds of post-health stability, and cold ready at 10,918ms against a 25,000ms budget. Immutable demo image: `ghcr.io/elizaos/eliza-demo@sha256:d34826f09d030965bd55418d88fbfd4e8904778ad98b0bf3debd934c4f096b13` (config `sha256:b7ff9e0b01962c3c09f6fef41a36ee12a3f740310770767900c70206c0d63315`). [Canonical attestation](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/attestations/39917519), [demo attestation](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/attestations/39917538), exact OCI revision, and credential-free pulls from both canonical and demo repositories were independently verified.
